title: The sideways postcard
description: First contact. A sorting office has stamped a postcard sideways. Compare the worked example, then predict the same stamp on a new arrangement. You do not need to identify stamps that never appear in the delivery.
hint: Follow a corner cell through the example. A clockwise quarter turn sends the top-left cell to the top-right.
explanation: A rotates the whole board 90 degrees clockwise. The first example is asymmetric, so it distinguishes this effect from the other seven operations. The other stamps remain unknown, but every surviving language agrees about the target.

title: A parcel that wraps
description: The night conveyor never drops a parcel off the edge. Learn stamp B from one pass, then deliver a board that uses B twice. Count each pass rather than treating the far edge as a wall.
hint: Each row wraps independently. Two right shifts equal one left shift on a three-cell row.
explanation: B shifts each row one cell right, wrapping its last cell to its first position. BB shifts twice. No parcel changes row or color. This is a repeated operation, not a single move of two cells without wrapping.

title: The empty demonstration
description: A diplomat offers a demonstration on a completely empty board. It looks convincing, but every operation leaves that board empty. Spend an experiment on an arrangement that can actually distinguish rules.
hint: Try A on an off-center, asymmetric board using more than one color. An empty input supplies no evidence.
explanation: A reflects across the main diagonal: row and column exchange places. The empty worked example removes none of the 1,680 mappings. A carefully chosen asymmetric experiment identifies A; repeating the empty experiment spends a query without adding evidence.

title: The red-only disguise
description: A laboratory paints every occupied cell red before demonstrating C. Two color rules give the same demonstration. Your final delivery contains blue and yellow as well; find an experiment that tells those rules apart.
hint: A blue cell is decisive: the color cycle makes it yellow, while swapping red and blue makes it red.
explanation: C cycles red to blue, blue to yellow and yellow to red; empty cells stay empty. A red-only demonstration cannot distinguish that from swapping red and blue. A blue or yellow test separates them. Applying the cycle twice is not an undo.

title: The center tells too little
description: The observatory puts one yellow light in the exact center and demonstrates D. Several spatial operations appear identical there. The final board has a much less convenient arrangement.
hint: Move evidence away from the center. A single red corner distinguishes a half turn from several reflections.
explanation: D rotates the board 180 degrees. The centered yellow light is preserved by the rotations and reflections, and also by the red/blue swap. An asymmetric colored probe is needed before assuming that no visible change means no rule.

title: The two-stamp detour
description: An express delivery uses A then B. Both stamps have examples, but copying their outputs side by side does not compose them. Start with the target board and apply the leftmost stamp first.
hint: A is a clockwise turn. B then shifts the rows of the already rotated board, not the original rows.
explanation: A is a quarter turn and B a wrapped right shift. AB gives [1,2,0,0,0,3,2,0,1] on this input. Reversing them would give [0,1,2,2,0,1,0,3,0]. The language applies programs from left to right.

title: Undo is not a name
description: A repair crew says that using A twice restores the board. That statement fits several different operations. Your target uses A once, so a double-stamp demonstration is not enough to choose a unique result.
hint: A half turn, either reflection and the red/blue swap all undo themselves. Test one A, not another AA.
explanation: A swaps red and blue while preserving yellow and empty cells. AA alone is compatible with multiple self-inverse operations. A single-stamp asymmetric probe distinguishes them. The result is judged against what the evidence actually determines.

title: A loop of three floors
description: The lift operator demonstrates BBB. Everything returns to its starting place. Your delivery asks for only one B, and the tower has three floors. Choose a probe that reveals the direction of travel.
hint: Wrapped shifts and the three-color cycle return after three applications. One B on an asymmetric multicolor board separates them.
explanation: B shifts the rows down by one, wrapping the bottom row to the top. BBB is the identity, but this observation also fits a right shift or a color cycle. A triple repetition can expose a period without identifying the underlying operation.

title: Paint after folding
description: A print shop demonstrates C and D separately. One changes position and the other changes color. Reconstruct a three-stamp print without adding an imaginary interaction between those independent effects.
hint: C mirrors left/right and D cycles colors. The two C operations undo one another.
explanation: C is a left/right mirror and D a color cycle. Spatial permutations commute with these global color substitutions. The two mirrors in CDC cancel, so its result equals D alone. Identifying that relationship can save a query.

title: A diagonal dispute
description: The archive labels two reflections with different stamps. Its examples use an asymmetric record, so the stamps can be separated. Your delivery uses the diagonal reflection followed by a left/right mirror.
hint: The main diagonal stays fixed under A. B reverses the columns of the board produced by A.
explanation: A transposes row and column, while B mirrors left/right. Applying both in order produces a clockwise quarter turn. Two different reflections can therefore compose to the same effect as a rotation, even though neither individual stamp is a rotation.

title: No spare copy of a rule
description: Every stamp has a different operation. Three stamps are demonstrated, and the last delivery uses the fourth. Use the injective rule constraint, but do not assume that four stamps must use all eight available operations.
hint: Knowing three stamps leaves five possible operations for D, not one. Probe D directly.
explanation: A, B and C are quarter turn, half turn and left/right mirror. D is the diagonal reflection, but five unused operations were initially available to it. Distinct assignments remove used choices without making the whole eight-operation menu mandatory.

title: The black-and-yellow loophole
description: A testing station avoids red and blue entirely when it demonstrates B. That hides the difference between leaving colors alone and swapping the two missing colors. Use a deliberate colored counterexample.
hint: A red/blue swap cannot be observed on a board containing only yellow and empty cells. Include red or blue in your experiment.
explanation: B swaps red and blue. The symmetric yellow pattern is also unchanged by several spatial rules, so its unchanged appearance does not identify a color-preserving operation. A red cell placed off the symmetry axes makes the missing distinction visible.

title: The combined receipt
description: A courier prints only AB on its receipt. It offers no single-stamp samples. Your final order is BA. Design a calibration that separates the two stamps instead of repeatedly measuring their combined effect.
hint: Single-stamp queries A and B on an asymmetric board are more direct than asking AB again.
explanation: A shifts right and B rotates clockwise. An AB observation can fit more than one pair, and reversing a pair need not preserve its output. Separating the component effects provides a stronger explanation than memorizing a combined example.

title: Color names are not coordinates
description: A theater changes every colored seat marker and then moves the entire seating chart. Learn both effects. The empty aisle cells must remain empty through the color changes.
hint: Two color cycles change red to yellow, blue to red and yellow to blue. Only then do rows wrap down.
explanation: A cycles the three nonempty colors and B shifts down. Empty is a separate value, never a fourth color in the cycle. AAB therefore applies two recolorings and one wrapped row move; it never creates or deletes a seat marker.

title: Same rules, different evidence
description: Two demonstrations of C use symmetric arrangements. They look like two independent clues, but may repeat the same weakness. Choose a third experiment for what it separates, not for how different its picture looks.
hint: Both examples are mirror-symmetric. Put different colors at the left and right edges of a row.
explanation: C mirrors left/right. Recoloring the same symmetric shape does not necessarily add spatial information. A good calibration breaks the symmetry responsible for the remaining ambiguity rather than merely changing the board cosmetically.

title: The eight-stamp shipment
description: A warehouse allows a maximum of eight stamps per delivery. This order uses the entire allowance. Keep an intermediate board or simplify repeated operations before reconstructing the final shipment.
hint: AAAA is four quarter turns, and BBB is three wrapped right shifts. Each group returns to its starting arrangement.
explanation: A is a quarter turn, B a right shift and C a color cycle. AAAA and BBB each cancel as complete periods, leaving C. A long program is not necessarily a difficult transformation if the period structure is used carefully.

title: One red pebble
description: A river station shows D acting on a single red corner pebble. The position is unchanged and the pebble becomes blue. That still leaves two color rules. Choose the smallest useful second color test.
hint: Test D on a blue or yellow pebble. Red alone cannot separate swapping from cycling.
explanation: D swaps red and blue and is its own inverse. DD restores every color. The red-only clue also fits a three-color cycle, whose double application would differ. A single well-chosen pebble can provide more information than a complicated all-red board.

title: Across the folded map
description: The survey team supplies A and C but leaves B unlabelled. Your delivery crosses the diagonal, shifts a row and crosses back. Infer only the missing effect, then respect the program order.
hint: Probe B. A diagonal reflection before and after a right shift converts its axis of motion.
explanation: A is the diagonal reflection and B a wrapped right shift. ABA is equivalent to a wrapped downward shift because the reflections exchange the row and column axes. C's color cycle is irrelevant to this target, even though its example is available.

title: A final that needs no query
description: The station refuses extra experiments. Its worked examples identify two stamps. Reconstruct ABBA from those facts. Unknown stamps C and D are not an excuse to guess.
hint: A mirror and a red/blue swap each undo themselves. The two B stamps are adjacent.
explanation: A mirrors left/right and B swaps red and blue. BB cancels, leaving AA, which also cancels. The final output equals its input. Many complete languages survive, but every one gives the same target; language identification and target identification are different goals.

title: The honest incomplete briefing
description: A stranded outpost gives only an empty demonstration and allows no experiments. The final message uses A on a colored asymmetric board. There is deliberately not enough evidence for one forced answer. Submit a defensible interpretation and inspect the ambiguity report.
hint: You cannot identify A from an empty input. Any output produced by one of the eight valid operations is consistent; inventing a new operation is not.
explanation: This mission intentionally remains ambiguous. A actually shifts down, but all eight operations fit the empty demonstration. The game accepts any reconstruction supported by a surviving language as consistent, without claiming that the hidden rule was uniquely deduced.

title: Two channels, one color cycle
description: The harbor routes parcels with A and recolors them with D. B and C also exist but have no role in the target. Reconstruct a mixed program while keeping spatial and color reasoning separate.
hint: A and D commute. ADAD is two right shifts and two color cycles.
explanation: A shifts right and D cycles colors. Reordering these independent effects does not change the output: two right shifts and two color cycles suffice. This commutation does not imply that arbitrary pairs of geometric stamps can also be reordered.

title: A mirror changes the route
description: A mountain guide demonstrates C, then provides a combined CD receipt. The final route is D alone. Use the known reflection to reason about the remaining operation, or spend an experiment to isolate it.
hint: C mirrors left/right. Compare the CD result with the board after C, rather than with the original input.
explanation: C is a left/right reflection and D a right shift. A combined example becomes a single-operation example once the known prefix has been applied. The intermediate board, rather than the original board, is the correct input when inferring D.

title: The unhelpful confirmation
description: A research team already knows A from an asymmetric example. Its second sample applies A to another board. Your target is BC, so another confirmation of A will not directly answer the new question. Allocate the remaining two experiments deliberately.
hint: Probe B and C separately on an asymmetric multicolor input. Repeating A cannot identify either unknown stamp.
explanation: A rotates clockwise, B shifts down and C swaps red and blue. Once A is uniquely identified, a second confirmation contributes no new mapping information. A query budget rewards experiments that address the target's unknown components.

title: Foundry final: teach the next visitor
description: The last station mixes color, geometry and a partially documented stamp. Reconstruct DBAC, inspect the surviving-language report, then use the builder to make a fork with better teaching examples. Preserve the source's rules when publishing a fork.
hint: A cycles colors, B reflects diagonally and C shifts right. An asymmetric D query fills the one missing piece.
explanation: D rotates clockwise. Apply D, then the diagonal reflection B, then color cycle A, then wrapped right shift C. A fork can improve which examples are taught or which final is asked while keeping the inherited mapping; a changed mapping is a new independent challenge, not the same source language.
